content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | Test Infrastructure & CI/CD
marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including two years focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has built ephemeral test environments using Docker Compose, Helm and a shared Kubernetes cluster. Seeking a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and infrastructure: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (basic)
Programming and scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Linux, Git, PostgreSQL, Grafana (test metrics dashboards)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer, Test Infrastructure | Odrava Health Software | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams of approximately 25 developers, covering builds, unit, integration and end-to-end tests, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand ephemeral environments.
- Built ephemeral test environments for merge requests, first with Docker Compose and later with Helm charts on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests, reducing the flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tools to seed test data into PostgreSQL.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications manually and through automation for client projects.
- Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist, 2nd Line | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

LANGUAGES
Polish: Native | English: C1 | German: A2

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clean, concise, professional, and easy to scan. It uses strong quantified achievements, especially the pipeline reduction from 38 to 14 minutes and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to under 1%. The progression from QA automation into test infrastructure is clear, and the experience bullets are substantially stronger than generic responsibility statements. However, the document currently presents the candidate primarily as a QA automation engineer seeking a transition, rather than as an infrastructure-focused engineer. It also does not demonstrate several central requirements of the role, including Terraform/Terragrunt, cloud infrastructure, networking, security, systems architecture, and stakeholder leadership. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: standard section headings, plain text structure, conventional chronology, no tables or graphics, and recognizable technology keywords. The title and skills section contain relevant terms such as CI/CD, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Linux, Python, Bash, Jenkins, and GitLab CI. AI and ATS screening probability for this specific role is moderate rather than high because the CV lacks the job's strongest screening terms: Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS or another cloud platform, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, systems architecture, and stakeholder engagement. These terms must not be added because they are not supported by the original candidate information. The existing supported infrastructure experience should instead be made more prominent and described using precise infrastructure and platform terminology.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on test infrastructure, CI/CD ownership, containerized environments, Kubernetes-based deployment environments, Linux, scripting, automation, observability through Grafana test dashboards, and measurable operational improvement. The ownership of GitLab CI for three product teams also provides some evidence of cross-team responsibility. The CV does not show strong Terraform and Terragrunt, cloud design or operation, AWS, systems architecture, networking or mTLS/SSL/TLS, practical security awareness, formal technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, IoT or remote-device integration, or virtual-machine experience. The Java experience is limited to test code rather than backend or full-stack development. These are genuine alignment gaps and cannot be solved through wording alone. The document should therefore position the candidate accurately as an infrastructure-oriented QA automation engineer with CI/CD and environment-engineering experience, without implying full readiness in unsupported areas.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: No factual hallucinations were identified, so no unsupported technologies or experience should be added.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the transition-focused wording "Seeking a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role" with a more capability-focused statement such as: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including two years focused on CI/CD pipeline ownership, test infrastructure, containerized environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI for three product teams and builds ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and Helm on Kubernetes." This keeps the summary truthful while presenting the candidate's existing infrastructure work more strongly.
2. In the Technical Skills section, change the category label "CI/CD and infrastructure" to "CI/CD, containerization and test infrastructure". This more accurately reflects the documented experience and avoids implying unsupported cloud infrastructure expertise.
3. In the Odrava Health Software experience, change "Built ephemeral test environments for merge requests, first with Docker Compose and later with Helm charts on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster" to "Built and maintained ephemeral test environments for merge requests, first with Docker Compose and later with Helm charts deployed to the company's shared Kubernetes cluster." This makes the operational/maintenance aspect explicit without claiming unsupported cloud ownership.
4. In the Odrava Health Software section, add the supported operational context to the pipeline bullet by changing it to: "Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams of approximately 25 developers, covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, artifact publishing and pipeline maintenance." Do not add claims about cloud deployment, production infrastructure, or system architecture.
5. In the Technical Skills section, retain "Kubernetes (basic)" and "Grafana (test metrics dashboards)" exactly or use the clearer wording "Kubernetes (basic; shared cluster test environments)" and "Grafana (test metrics dashboards)". This improves keyword context while avoiding overstatement.
6. In the Brightmill Software House QA Engineer entry, make the Java experience more ATS-readable without overstating it by changing "Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite" to "Introduced an automated regression suite using Selenium and Java test code for the largest client project." This accurately signals JVM-related experience while making clear that it was test code, not backend development.
7. In the Professional Summary or the first Odrava bullet, use the supported phrase "cross-team ownership" only if tied to the existing evidence. For example: "Provides cross-team ownership of GitLab CI pipelines used by three product teams." Do not describe this as technical leadership, stakeholder management, or leading architecture because those capabilities are not evidenced in the source material.
